scenes.title: 1968 Michigan Tachistoscope Lab: 0 to 25 Flashes of 'IKTITAF' & Calligraphic Symbols Turn Neutral Nonsense Into 'Wonderful'!
scenes.era: 1968, Research Center for Group Dynamics, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1968 Michigan cognitive laboratory featuring a brushed-aluminum **slide projection screen and tachistoscope viewer**, stimulus cards displaying **nonsense Turkish words ('IKTITAF' — Shown 25x vs 'BIWONJNI' — Shown 1x)** alongside **calligraphic ideographs and yearbook portraits**, and a bold rising **Logarithmic Liking Curve Board (0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25 Exposures -> 'Goodness' Rating 2.9 to 4.5+)**.

positions.who: Robert Zajonc (mannequin in 1968 crisp dark suit, white shirt, and narrow tie)
positions.where: standing beside the projection screen and Logarithmic Liking Curve pointing from the 25x 'IKTITAF' card to the top of the Goodness rating curve

positions.who: Two Michigan Undergraduate mannequins (in 1968 collegiate V-neck sweaters at wooden rating desks)
positions.where: marking 'IKTITAF (25x) = Very Good!' and 'BIWONJNI (0x) = Neutral/Low' on their semantic-differential sheets despite zero translation!

props.name: stimulus flash cards ('IKTITAF 25x' | Calligraphic Character 25x | Yearbook Portrait 25x)
props.period_detail: displays Zajonc's exact 3 stimulus families from the 1968 Monograph

props.name: Logarithmic Exposure-Liking Graph ('0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 5 -> 10 -> 25 Views')
props.period_detail: visualizes steep early warmth gains tapering gracefully at high counts

actions.verb_sequence: flashes neutral nonsense words and calligraphic characters across 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, and 25 exposures -> Students rate what each unknown symbol 'means' -> Every stimulus family climbs smoothly up the Good/Warm scale purely from repetition!

reactions.reaction: laugh surprised upon learning 'IKTITAF' and 'BIWONJNI' were randomly counterbalanced across classrooms
smiles noting 'Familiarity breeds affection long before memory catches up'

scenes.wardrobe: 1968 American university attire: tailored charcoal suit and narrow tie; collegiate cardigan and V-neck sweaters.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key Ann Arbor laboratory daylight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Flash a totally meaningless word like 'IKTITAF' twenty-five times, and college students swear it means something noble and wonderful — swap which class gets the 25 flashes and the opposite nonsense word wins!

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1968 Michigan psychology classroom where Robert Zajonc points from flashed 'IKTITAF 25x' and calligraphic symbol cards to a rising 0-to-25 logarithmic liking graph before seated students

scenes.title: 1-Millisecond Subliminal Proof: Liking Without Remembering!

layout.description: Crisp optical viewer flashing irregular octagons for 1 millisecond alongside a 50% Recognition vs 60% Liking split bar.

positions.where: scoring pure 50% guesswork on 'Which shape did I see?' yet reliably picking the old shape on 'Which shape do I LIKE?'

actions.verb_sequence: flashes shape for 1 ms -> Participant fails memory test -> still chooses flashed shape as prettier

scenes.recognition_hook: Flash a shape for one-thousandth of a second so memory hits 50% pure guesswork — and people STILL pick that exact shape as the prettier one!

scenes.title: Why You Love Your Mirror Face & Hate Group Photos (Mita et al. 1977)
scenes.era: Modern sunlit bathroom mirror & living room table

layout.description: Bright split comparison showing a Mirror-Reversed Portrait ('Preferred by Self: 68%') beside a True Camera Portrait ('Preferred by Friends!').

positions.where: pointing to opposite flips of the exact same face based on which orientation each person sees every day!

props.name: Mirror-Flipped vs True-Orientation Portrait Pair
props.period_detail: instantly relatable real-world proof of Mere Exposure

actions.verb_sequence: picks mirror-flipped portrait (seen 10,000 mornings) -> Best friend picks true unflipped portrait (seen across coffee tables)

scenes.recognition_hook: You don't look bad in photos — you've just seen your mirror-flipped face 10,000 times, while your friends fell in love with the unflipped original!

scenes.title: Spaced Familiarity vs Overexposure Boredom

layout.description: Warm table showing 'Give New Healthy Foods & Ideas 8 Spaced Tries' alongside 'Don't Mistake 25 Ad Impressions for Truth'.

positions.where: introducing a new vegetable / unfamiliar genre across spaced calm days until fluency blooms into genuine liking

props.name: Spaced 1-to-10 Exposure Tracker
props.period_detail: applies Zajonc + Bornstein's inverted-U spacing rule

actions.verb_sequence: spaces 8 calm exposures -> initial unfamiliarity melts into genuine enjoyment

scenes.recognition_hook: Give good new habits eight spaced tries before quitting — and never let 25 ad impressions fool your fluency meter into trusting hype!
